Bracco submitted this NDA using the same confirmatory clinical study data (three phase 3 studies) submitted back in 2001 but now with updated safety data and the results of a recently completed study that examined the effects of Sonovue upon pulmonary hemodynamics.

design.text: Multi-center controlled trials in which each patient received randomized-order intravenous bolus injections of Lumason; contrast echocardiography compared to non-contrast (baseline) echocardiography in the same patient, with images evaluated by two independent blinded reviewers.

citations.quote: In Studies A and B, each patient received four intravenous bolus injections of Lumason (0.5, 1, 2, and 4 mL), in randomized order. In Study C, each patient received two doses of Lumason (1 mL and 2 mL) in randomized order. All three studies assessed endocardial border delineation and left ventricular opacification. For each patient in each study, echocardiography with Lumason was compared to non-contrast (baseline) echocardiography.

population.text: 191 patients with suspected cardiac disease and suboptimal non-contrast echocardiography (127 men, 64 women; mean age 59 years).

citations.quote: A total of 191 patients with suspected cardiac disease and suboptimal non-contrast echocardiography received Lumason in three multi-center controlled clinical trials (76 patients in Study A, 62 patients in Study B, and 53 patients in Study C). Among these patients, there were 127 men and 64 women. The mean age was 59 years (range 22 to 96 years).

endpoint.text: Improvement in left ventricular endocardial border delineation (and left ventricular opacification) with contrast versus baseline non-contrast echocardiography.

citations.quote: All three studies assessed endocardial border delineation and left ventricular opacification.

n.text: N=191 (Study A 76, Study B 62, Study C 53)

citations.quote: A total of 191 patients with suspected cardiac disease and suboptimal non-contrast echocardiography received Lumason in three multi-center controlled clinical trials (76 patients in Study A, 62 patients in Study B, and 53 patients in Study C).

result.text: In all three studies Lumason improved left ventricular endocardial border delineation; the percentage of patients with inadequate border delineation (Reader A) fell from 79% to 33% in Study A, 50% to 19% in Study B, and 23% to 19% in Study C. Complete left ventricular opacification was observed in 52% to 80% of patients after a 2.0-mL dose.

citations.quote: In all three studies, complete left ventricular opacification was observed in 52% to 80% of the patients following administration of a 2.0-mL dose of Lumason.

indication.text: Ultrasound contrast agent indicated for use in patients with suboptimal echocardiograms to opacify the left ventricular chamber and to improve the delineation of the left ventricular endocardial border.

citations.quote: Lumason is indicated for use in patients with suboptimal echocardiograms to opacify the left ventricular chamber and to improve the delineation of the left ventricular endocardial border.

target_moa.text: Within the blood, the acoustic impedance of Lumason microspheres is lower than that of surrounding tissue, so an ultrasound beam is reflected from the microsphere/tissue interface; the reflected signal provides a visual image contrasting the blood from surrounding tissues. The microspheres are an SF6 gas core surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer shell.

citations.quote: Within the blood, the acoustic impedance of Lumason microspheres is lower than that of the surrounding non-aqueous tissue. Therefore, an ultrasound beam is reflected from the interface between the microspheres and the surrounding tissue. The reflected ultrasound signal provides a visual image that shows a contrast between the blood and the surrounding tissues.

The sulfur hexafluoride lipid microspheres are composed of \text{SF}_6 gas in the core surrounded by an outer shell monolayer of phospholipids consisting of DSPC and DPPG-Na with palmitic acid as a stabilizer.

modality.text: Other (ultrasound contrast agent: gas-filled lipid microspheres)

citations.quote: Lumason is a new molecular entity classified as an ultrasound contrast agent.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥0.5%) are headache (0.9%) and nausea (0.6%); overall adverse reactions occurred in 302 (4.9%) of 6179 patients. Serious cardiopulmonary reactions, including fatalities, have occurred uncommonly within 30 minutes of administration (boxed warning). Anaphylactoid reactions have uncommonly been observed.

Serious cardiopulmonary reactions, including fatalities, have occurred uncommonly during or following the injection of ultrasound contrast agents, including sulfur hexafluoride lipid microspheres (5.1). Most serious reactions occur within 30 minutes of administration (5.1).

Anaphylactoid reactions such as skin erythema, rash, urticaria, flushing, throat tightness, dyspnea, or anaphylactic shock have uncommonly been observed following the injection of Lumason. These reactions may occur in patients with no history of prior exposure to sulfur hexafluoride lipid containing microspheres.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA (2803-1): Conduct a multicenter clinical evaluation of safety and efficacy of Lumason as a contrast agent in pediatric echocardiography in patients ages 9-17 years, evaluating efficacy of Lumason contrasted echocardiography vs. non-contrast echocardiography for left ventricular border delineation in 92 patients, with pharmacokinetic assessments in 6 patients ages 9-12 years and 6 patients ages 12-17 years.

citations.quote: **2803-1** Deferred pediatric study under PREA: Conduct a multicenter clinical evaluation of safety and efficacy in pediatric patients ages 9-17 years of age of Lumason as a contrast agent in pediatric echocardiography. Evaluate the efficacy of Lumason contrasted echocardiography vs. non-contrast echocardiography for left ventricular border delineation in 92 patients (males and females) 9-17 years old. During the clinical evaluation, pharmacokinetic assessments will be performed on 6 patients, 9-12 years old (3 males and 3 females) and 6 patients 12-17 years old (3 males and 3 females).

citations.quote: On April 11, 2014 Bracco Diagnostics resubmitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for Lumason (sulfur hexafluoride lipid-Type A microsphere) in response to a November 30, 2013 complete response action taken because of manufacturing deficiencies identified by the agency during the inspection of the Bracco manufacturing facility.

summary.text: Lumason was approved as a new molecular entity ultrasound contrast agent via a 505(b)(1) NDA originally submitted December 21, 2011. It received two Complete Response Letters for manufacturing facility deficiencies before the April 11, 2014 resubmission led to approval; no advisory committee meeting was needed and a deferred pediatric study was required under PREA.
